name: sort
plain: `sort` puts lines in order. With options it can sort numbers, dates, columns and versions, remove duplicates, check whether a file is sorted, or shuffle lines at random.
It is half of the classic counting trick: sort | uniq -c | sort -rn, which ranks anything in a log from most to least common.
when: Rank the most common IP, user or path in a log.
Sort a table by one column, numbers by size, or file sizes from du.

examples.title: Numbers as text vs as numbers  (-n)
Sort by a column with a separator  (-t -k)
Check whether a file is sorted  (-c)

mistakes: Language settings change the order: LC_ALL=C sort gives plain byte order, which scripts and uniq usually expect.
uniq only removes neighbouring duplicates: sort first.
-k2 means from field 2 to the end of the line: use -k2,2 to sort on field 2 only.
